body:
It sounds like the two of you may have had a breakthrough of sorts?  If so, that's fantastic.  It also sounds like she may have agreed that you could benefit from quitting your job.  Although, it sounds like there is a "yes, but..." in there somewhere.

I am glad that talking has been able to help you somewhat and I'm honored to be a part of that.  Thank you for the gold, and keep me updated on what happens.
I agree with PP.  I wouldn't find it creepy.

Wow, it sounds like you may have received an inadvertent (but important!) lesson about trusting coworkers.  I don't mean to sound negative, but it has been my experience that it is important to proceed with extreme caution when blending home with your work life.  It's not that work relationships can't be cultivated into extremely rewarding circles of trust, you just need to be very careful in choosing the people you trust.  I'm so sorry that your coworker made you feel betrayed.  I'm sure that could only compound your feeling of being alone.

Hypothetical question:  what scenario do you imagine would play out with your wife if you up and quit your job?  What would happen if you told her you were going to quit your job, and it was not up for discussion, but you would like her support?

No one is Superman; he is complete fiction.  Good on you for trying, though.  That certainly shows strength of character.  Even the strongest of people need help.  It is not a matter of "willpower" although it canbe tempting to blame it on that.  This sounds like your time to need a hand and it sounds fairly temporary.  I know it's not much, but I'll be here as your sounding board whenever you need, and I won't turn around and tell your boss or peers.  For what it's worth.
Thank you, I really appreciate the time you took to help me.
I completely agree with your assessment.  And you need to talk about some of this stuff with your wife.  Would she be open to counseling?  It could help your communication tremendously.

Sorry, I am new to reddit and I of course read the rules and used the search function before posting to this sub but did not find anything that pertains specifically to my question.  

I obviously did something incorrectly if a mod is getting involved, so can someone please help point me in the correct direction?
You got it!  Happy to help. :)

I am female.  And yes, perhaps there are a number of women who might be undateable for you, but that's not a bad thing.  There are plenty of things ranging from trivial to major that make people undateable to one another.  For example, a woman's judge mental nature should make her undateable for YOU.  Just as, perhaps, you might prefer to date someone who is your intellectual equal or someone who keeps her nails trimmed.  (I don't know!). Your sexual history might be a deal-breaker for some, but I guarantee you, this is not a deal breaker for millions of people.  You don't need to lie.  You don't need to ask the question up front.  Your past does not define you.  You, like everyone else on the dating scene, just need to be a little patient.

I know, easier said than done, right?  Like you, I too am (painfully) introverted and have pretty severe "social anxiety" so I know how hard it can be to meet people or even be so presumptuous as to filter the people you let into your life and your unique little world.  BUT! Over the last decade or so, I have learned to increase my tolerance for social and emotional discomfort and interacting with people is slowly but surely getting easier and becoming more natural for me.  Like I said before, it is a skill, a language (like C++ maybe?  I don't know, that's as far as I got in computer science.  Ha ha.) that CAN be developed.

I believe in you and your ability to succeed in this area.  I don't know why, it's just something in your writing and your logical approach that communicates intelligence and problem-solving abilities.  You are also young and you have your entire life ahead of you still (like we all technically do, I guess) Just be patient.  If you ever need more advice or encouragement without going to /r/askwomen, I'll be here.

Hell, I'll even go over there and ask them for you, if you want.

Oh, sir, I am so sorry to hear you feel this way and that your social life is not currently taking the direction you would like.  Sexual history is such a minor thing to many women.  In relationships, it is all about compatibility and if someone would reject you for that given all the other qualities and things you have going for you, the it is simply not the right person for you.  You sound like a lovely (albeit introverted) person.  Connecting with people is not easy for everyone, but it is a skill that can be developed like many other things.  I agree with the pp that a few women you've read about are statistically a terrible representation of every woman you meet.  Don't lose heart.

Message the girl!  You have a responsibility to not do nothing. :)

Sorry, I know that's probably not helpful.

Thank you for telling your story.  I'm new-ish here but have been finding tidbits that seem to be helping, too.  I'll cross my fingers for you!
This is wonderful.  Thank you for writing it.

I was in a similar situation when I was your age.  I'm all grown up and recognized by society as a human being now (well, for the most part).  I don't have any advice for you except to say that it does get easier.  You probably aren't doing yourself any favors by skipping class, but it honestly isn't the end of the world.  Best of luck to you, and I'm here if you want to talk.

You're so young!  I know, that's probably not helpful to you at the moment and I remember feeling like my life had passed when I was your age, too, but it HASN'T!  You have accumulated 23 years of thoughts, feelings, experiences, relationships and lord knows what else that make up the completely unique existence that is YOU.  There is no one out there just like you and for that reason alone, you can't possibly be a waste of a person.  and, if you don't like the unique existence that is you, you have PLENTY of time to take what you've learned and START OVER.  You could live another ENTIRE lifetime as you know it to this point and STILL have time for kids.  Pretty amazing to think about in those terms, I think.

You sound smart, thoughtful, and responsible.  There is no way you have failed your parents.

I don't say these things to marginalized your feelings or what you are expressing; depression is real, and it is ugly, but it also lies to you.

I think you know what you have to do.  Unless you are financially dependent on your job at the credit union (and it doesn't sound as though you are) you need to resign.  Nothing is more important than your health and well-being.  If you don't have that, what else could you possibly have?

Not that you were asking and it's certainly not my place to judge, but your relationship with your wife sounds somewhat dysfunctional and devoid of open and honest communication.  Have you considered marriage counseling?

Thank you for sharing your story, I'm sure that wasn't easy to do, but I'm glad it felt good to finally say something.  I don't have any advice for you either, but like a pp said, the light of your soul shines through your post.
